questions.q: The normal bacteria residing in the human body are called:

options.e: Correct. These are the commensal community of the body.
Wrong. Probiotics are beneficial bacteria taken as supplements or foods.

questions.q: Who first observed live microorganisms, which he called animalcules?

options.e: Wrong. Known for pure cultures and the germ theory.
Correct. He used simple microscopes to see microbes in teeth scrapings and rain water.

questions.q: Who developed binomial nomenclature?

options.e: Wrong. Known for pasteurization and vaccines.
Correct. He is the father of modern taxonomy.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed the germ theory of disease and disproved spontaneous generation?

options.e: Correct. He linked microbes to disease and fermentation.
Wrong. Discovered viruses and nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

questions.q: Heating a liquid to kill bacteria is known as:

options.e: Wrong. Repeated boiling and cooling to kill spores.
Wrong. Use of chemicals on living tissue.

questions.q: John Tyndall is credited with:

options.t: Sterilization by repeated boiling and cooling
options.e: Correct. This kills microbes and their spores.

questions.q: Who is the father of modern antiseptic surgery, using phenol (carbolic acid)?

options.e: Correct. He applied germ theory to surgery.

questions.q: Robert Koch is best known for:

options.t: Isolating bacteria in pure culture and proving specific microbes cause specific diseases

questions.q: Martinus Beijerinck's two major discoveries were:

options.t: Tobacco mosaic virus and nitrogen-fixing bacteria
options.e: Correct. Both are credited to Beijerinck.

questions.q: Who discovered bacteriophages?

options.e: Correct. Bacteriophages infect and replicate within bacteria.

questions.q: Which year and scientist match the smallpox vaccine?

options.e: Correct. Jenner developed the first vaccine.

questions.q: Which pair is correctly matched?

questions.q: Which branch of microbiology studies fungi?

options.e: Correct. Mycology is the study of fungi.
